topics.topic: How signal-related, server-failure, and cleanup outcomes are classified as SERVED or SERVER_FAILED after listening
questions: Which outcome takes precedence when SIGINT or SIGTERM causes the web server to return but the process then ends because shutdown or cleanup fails, or when a server failure and the signal occur concurrently; and what observable condition proves that the server returned because of the signal?

When a server failure and SIGINT or SIGTERM overlap, what determines whether the server returned because of the signal: the first event, the return value or exception, the presence of any received signal, or an explicit shutdown cause recorded by the signal handler?
When the named signal makes the web server return but a later shutdown or cleanup step fails, which condition has precedence?
Must the server call actually return normally for SERVED, or does any process termination caused by SIGINT or SIGTERM after listening count as SERVED?

quotes:
The service has served once its web server has begun
listening. `ServiceExit` is START_FAILED, value `start_failed`: the process ends before it listens,
whatever ends it, a signal included; SERVED, value `served`: after it has served, the web server
returns because a SIGINT or SIGTERM stopped it; and SERVER_FAILED, value `server_failed`: after it has
served, the process ends in any other way.
judgement.divergence: One implementation returns SERVED/status 0 whenever SIGINT or SIGTERM caused the web server to return, even if cleanup later fails; another returns SERVER_FAILED/status 1 when a cleanup failure or concurrent server failure ultimately ends the process, which the process supervisor notices.
judgement.why: The passage does not establish precedence between a signal-caused server return and a later or concurrent failure.

witness.initial: The web server has begun listening.
events: The web server returns because SIGTERM stopped it.
A shutdown or cleanup step fails and ends the process.
outcomes: The outcome is SERVED with status 0 because SIGTERM caused the web server to return.
The outcome is SERVER_FAILED with status 1 because the process ended through the later failure.
witness.observer: The process supervisor observing the exit status.
basis:

returns because a SIGINT or SIGTERM stopped it; and SERVER_FAILED, value `server_failed`: after it has
served, the process ends in any other way.

topics.topic: Which signals must map to exit status 1 and how signal termination is translated into that status
questions: Does “a signal included” include signals that the process cannot handle or convert into status 1, and if so, what component must translate signal termination into the declared exit status?

Which signals are included, when must handlers be installed, and does the required status 1 replace the operating system's normal signal-derived status when a signal terminates the process before listening?

Does the status 1 mapped to START_FAILED have to be the actual operating-system process exit status for every signal, including an uncatchable signal, or is EXIT_STATUSES used only when the process can return an outcome?

quotes: run_service: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST call load_runtime_settings, then load_config with those settings, then read_token with the credential_file of the settings as a Path, then the imported create_app with that context and token, in that order, and serve the application with the imported uvicorn on the host of the imported BIND_HOST constant and the port of the settings, trusting no forwarded or proxy header. It MUST return the status of the row of the imported EXIT_STATUSES constant for the member of = models.ServiceExit the way the process ends: the START_FAILED member when any step or a signal ends it before the web server listens, after writing one line naming the failed step to standard error and never the token; the SERVED member when its web server returns after a SIGINT or SIGTERM stopped it; and the SERVER_FAILED member for any other end after the web server has begun listening.
judgement.why: The later service note assigns translation to run_service and requires it to return the START_FAILED row's status when a signal ends the process before listening.

topics.topic: The exact observable serving boundary between START_FAILED and post-serving outcomes
questions: Which observable event is the exact transition from START_FAILED to the post-serving outcomes: the operating-system socket entering listen state, successful bind, framework startup completion, entry into the accept loop, or another named event?

Which observable event is the exact boundary between START_FAILED and a post-service outcome: completion of the socket listen operation, successful binding of every configured socket, the server's readiness notification, or some other event?

quotes:
The service has served once its web server has begun
listening.
judgement.divergence: One implementation changes to post-serving outcomes when the operating-system socket enters the listening state; another waits for framework startup or readiness completion, so the process supervisor can observe status 0 versus status 1 for a signal arriving between those events.
judgement.why: The text names beginning to listen but does not identify the observable server event that constitutes that boundary.

witness.initial: The server has created a socket but has not completed its framework startup sequence.
events: The socket enters the operating-system listening state.
Before the framework reports startup complete, the operator sends SIGTERM.
outcomes: The service had served, so the outcome is SERVED with status 0.
The service had not yet served, so the outcome is START_FAILED with status 1.
witness.observer: The process supervisor observing the exit status.
basis:
The service has served once its web server has begun
listening.

topics.topic: Definition and exhaustive members of the models.ServiceExit enumeration
questions: Where is the `models.ServiceExit` enumeration defined, and is its exhaustive member set exactly START_FAILED=`start_failed`, SERVED=`served`, and SERVER_FAILED=`server_failed`? The supplied model text defines no such enumeration, while A8 depends on it.
Make the three members and their values an actual `models.ServiceExit` enumeration; leave A8 to define the imported `EXIT_STATUSES` policy table and any behavioral meaning keyed by that model enum.

returns because a SIGINT or SIGTERM stopped it; and SERVER_FAILED, value `server_failed`: after it has

topics.topic: How PublicationMark.marked_at is sourced, represented, sampled, and clock-read
questions: What authority supplies `marked_at`, in what datetime representation is it stored, at what event is it sampled, and how many clock readings may one mark operation take?

judgement.why: P2 judged the same question about the source, representation, sampling point and read count of PublicationMark.marked_at, and the relevant passages have not changed.

precedent.topic: Time source, representation, read timing, and read count for PublicationMark.marked_at
quotes:
1. The system clock is the one source of the current time, declared as `rules.time_source_policy`
   and reaching code through `system_clock_backend` as the operation `utc_now`.

2. Only a mark reads it, once, after the token, the request form and the identifiers are accepted and
   before the connection is examined or the project lock is taken. A mark refused before that point does
   not read it. A mark refused after it, and a replayed mark, have read it and write nothing. Scan, delivery
   and the health answer never read it.

3. The current time is a `datetime` in UTC without an offset, with microsecond precision and no
   rounding, written in ISO 8601 form as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`, followed by `.` and six digits when
   the microseconds are not zero, with no offset. Every instant of a record and an answer is written
   so. It sets `marked_at`.

- INV-13: a counting clock is read once by a mark and not at all by a scan, a delivery or the health answer (`test_only_the_mark_reads_the_clock`), and `marked_at` equals that reading (`test_a_marked_photo_is_reported_as_published`).
precedent.why: The clock source, representation, reading point and Required tests passage are unchanged from the closed State 2, and the credential/environment-setting changes did not make this topic matter.

topics.topic: Whether the file modification instant is captured once and reused for photo-time decisions
questions: Is the file modification instant captured exactly once per placement and reused both for camera-time plausibility checks and as the fallback photo moment, or may it be read again?

quotes:
A file that is read takes its modification time from one metadata reading of the file that was
opened, the one whose bytes are read, taken after the opening and before the read; A7 rule 4 gives its
form, and a delivery uses that time under A2 rule 3.
judgement.why: The text requires one metadata reading of the opened file and requires delivery, including A2's comparison and fallback, to use that time.
